title: Phased Versioning & Migration Playbook for Model API and Runtime Compatibility
creator: Amelia Park
description: Define and execute a low-risk, multi-phase versioning and deprecation rollout for breaking API/runtime changes and model-compatibility upgrades. This ticket owns the cross-functional playbook: migration windows, release notes cadence, SDK and console changes, partner comms, and rollback criteria. Focus area: provide deterministic timelines and tooling so customers can migrate with minimal disruption and predictable cost/latency outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Published public migration timeline and deprecation calendar for affected endpoints and model variants
Release notes template and coordinated cadence confirmed with Marketing and Docs
Migration scripts and compatibility test suite available in the repo and linked in docs
Canary rollout + automatic fallback behavior defined and validated in staging
Customer-facing migration guide and FAQ drafted and reviewed
All required approvals obtained (Security, Legal, Support, Sales enablement)

tasks: Inventory endpoints, models, and runtime flags impacted by change
Draft migration guide: code snippets, CLI scripts, and config flags
Coordinate release notes and blog draft with Marketing and Docs
Add SDK deprecation warnings and automated codemod where feasible
Create compatibility test harness and add to CI gates
Design Console UX for deprecation banners and per-route migration status
Prepare customer communications: developer-facing email, changelog, and account-level notices
Train Support and Solutions on migration troubleshooting and rollback steps
Define monitoring/success metrics and rollback thresholds
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Large customers on pinned legacy models may miss communications - Mitigation: account team outreach and dedicated migration SLA
Risk: Unexpected latency regressions during rollout - Mitigation: gradual canary + auto-fallback to compatible variant
Risk: SDK ecosystems lag behind server changes - Mitigation: ship SDK compatibility layer and warnings before enforcement
Risk: Docs or sample code mismatch - Mitigation: single source-of-truth in docs repo and pre-merge doc sign-off requirement
comms_plan: Week -6: Public migration calendar published on status.redwood.ai and blog post
Week -5: Release notes + in-console banners for affected routes
Week -4: SDK release with codemods and migration examples; email to users who used affected endpoints
Week -2: Webinar + office hours for enterprise customers; dedicated migration slack channel
Enforcement day: short notice reminder 48h and rollback channel open for incident response
Post-migration: one-week follow-up report with metrics and any outstanding customer tickets
rollback_plan: Immediate: toggle per-region routing to last compatible model variant
If repeated failures in canary: stop rollout and revert runtime flags; notify stakeholders
Post-revert: incident review, patch, and extend deprecation window by at least two weeks
metrics_and_success_criteria: <1% increase in 95th latency compared to baseline during canary
<0.5% error-rate regression attributable to breaking change during full rollout
>80% of active customers migrated or acknowledged migration plan within the first deprecation window
SDK adoption: 60% of active SDK users upgrade to compatibility release within 30 days
